page.layout: One page of running text, with a line of italic verse set inside the first paragraph and a chapter heading (XXXV, with its title) in the middle. Two marginal notes stand in the left margin, beside the first paragraphs. The right margin is empty.

main_text.p: Sanctè id Romanorum antiquo mori observatum, ut civilis belli victoriam luctuoso silentio, intra sinum gaudentes, involverent. Unde illa Lucani exclamatio:

p.i: Bella geri placuit nullos habitura triumphos!

main_text.p: Triumphi limites, Cæfar victis luculenta victoria in Macedonia, & deinde Africa, qui arma contra tulerant Romanis civibus; nullum de iis, quatuor de externis, Gallia, Ægypto, Pharnace, Juba, triumphos egit. Suetonius in Julio: Dio Cassius libro 43. Minori in victoria, Pifone judi-ciariis armis post Sentiana debellato, Tiberius pari moderatione usus: cum Valerius Mesallinus signum aureum in æde Martis ultoris, Cacina Severus aram ultioni statuendam censuissent, prohibuit: ob externas ea victorias sacrari dicitans, domestica mala tristitia operienda. Quod ad privatæ vitæ conditionem referens vir sapiens, aut jurgio inter necessarios abstinebit, aut de victoria non gloriabitur.
main_text.head: Fato, non dignitate apiscentis, impe-ria conferuntur.
main_text.p: Claudii fatum Claudius, qui tredecim per annos orbi Romano leges daturus erat, tanta obscuritate, vel contemptu potiùs, in aula Tiberiana latuit, ut fratrem eum Ger-manici, cujus de vindicta gratulandum erat, index imprudens præteriret. Idem Claudius Cajo imperanti non despicatui modo, qui eum sævitiæ furentis principis eripuit, verum irrisui etiam ob tarditatem ingenii, & aulico ludibrio fuit. Nō immerito igitur Cornelius in hæc ingeniosæ admirationis verba erumpit: Mihi quanto plura recentium, seu veterum revolvo, tanto magis ludibria rerum mortalium cum-ctis in negotiis obversantur. quippe fama, spe, venera-tione potiùs omnes destinabantur imperio, quàm quem futurum principem fortuna in occulto tenebat. Quod-que mirandum magis est; illo sub caudice, illo sub stipite principe nec quicquam res Romana adversi con-cepit, & accessu Britanniæ adaucta est. Nec veri modum in laudatione funebri Nero excessit: nihil regen-[?]

page.notes: The text ends with a printed ornament or symbol after "regen-" that I could not read; it is not transcribed. The word after the hyphen is taken from the catchword "tes" at the foot, so "regen-" with [?] is my best reading. Possible printing or reading doubts: "Ger-manici" and "impe-ria" are hyphenated at line ends as printed. The long s has been written as s throughout, so forms such as "sacrari", "despicatui" and "irrisui" are read from context. The printed "potiùs" and "quàm" keep their accents as printed.
